habitat: Singly or in pairs in eastern evergreen forest, riparian forest and dense woodland, in the mid-stratum, hawking from a perch.
summary: A common, localised resident. Black, with ruby-red eyes and splayed outer tail feathers, but only a shallow fork. The call is a loud cherit cherit or cherit-wit-wit, with other strident sounds and imitations. The stub has no Kemp estimate and none was added.

similar.note: Fork-tailed Drongo has a deep fork. This bird has the same splayed outer feathers but only a shallow indentation.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.

tail.shape: Splayed outer feathers with only a shallow fork.

viewNotes.note: Black, with a ruby-red eye and only a shallow fork in the tail.
Black underparts and a ruby-red eye.
The tail has splayed outer feathers and only a shallow indentation.
It hawks from a perch. A separate flight pattern was not described.
Black below. The underside of the wing was not named.

calls.description: A loud cherit! cherit! or cherit-wit-wit, plus other strident sounds and imitations. Newman does not separate the sexes. Grade A call from Satara, Kruger. The filename is kleinbyvanger-satara.mp3, the Afrikaans name.
